summary:
Hopscotch is a children’s game played around the world. Players toss a small marker into numbered spaces drawn on the ground, hop through the course while avoiding the marked space, retrieve the marker, and return. A missed throw, line touch, missed square, or loss of balance ends a turn. The first player to complete every numbered space wins. The game provides physical and cognitive exercise.

Its origin is unknown. Claims of ancient versions lack evidence, while written references in English date to the 17th century. The court’s shape and rules vary by region, and the game has many local names and forms. Some versions add rules for claiming squares or kicking the marker.

Hopscotch remains common in playgrounds worldwide. During the COVID-19 pandemic, a nearly 1,000-square court was created in Edinburgh for socially distanced play. The game has also inspired works of popular culture, including Julio Cortázar’s 1963 novel, whose chapters can be read in different orders.
